title: Applied Seller Adjustment
description: Record of one change the seller applied to a live media buy within a seller_adjustable_terms entry. It is the readback in get_media_buys applied_adjustments[] and its adjustment_id is the notification_id of media_buy.allowance_applied. Each application advances the buy's revision, as every committed change does. The revision history entry records the origin in actor (seller_system for automation, seller_operator when a person applied it), plus allowance_id and reason, and the account change feed record carries the same origin.kind, allowance_id and reason. Experimental in AdCP 3.3 (media_buy.seller_adjustment_allowances).

adjustment_id.description: Seller-assigned identifier, unique within the seller's account namespace (it is the notification_id) and stable across re-emissions.

allowance_id.description: The seller_adjustable_terms entry in the accepted commercial_terms that authorized this change.

revision.description: The media buy revision this application created.

reason.description: Short machine-readable reason code, such as forecast_shortfall; the same shape as the reason on an account change record. Human-readable text goes in the history entry's summary.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the purchase, as declared by the term.

package_id.description: The package the changed purchase maps to, when the seller assigned one.

previous_value.description: The value at path before this change.

value.description: The value at path after this change.

cumulative_change.description: Numeric fields: the absolute total change from the value in the accepted terms, including this one. Lets a buyer check max_change_fraction.

alternate_index.description: Position in the term's constraint.alternates[] that was used, when the change selected an alternate.

skipped_alternates.description: Earlier alternates that were not used, each with why it was unavailable, so the first-available rule is auditable.

examples.description: A budget release applied within a 20% reduce-only term
